cards.text: This one's a song, a psalm of David, Israel's king, and he's talking straight to God with no warm-up. He opens with this: "My heart is steadfast, O God…" And friend, he means it.

cards.question: True or false: With his heart steadfast, David says he will sing and make music with all his being.

cards.text: Then David calls out, "Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn." Friend, most of us are out here negotiating with the snooze button, and this man is waking up the MORNING.

cards.question: David's not keeping this song to himself. Where does he say he'll praise the LORD?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.question: David says why he's singing like this: God's loving devotion. How far does David say God's loving devotion reaches?

answers.text: To the edge of the sea

cards.text: Beyond the heavens, up to the clouds, and I spent YEARS thinking the lid of a junk drawer was the sky. Then David's praise turns into a prayer: "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens…"

cards.question: True or false: David prays that God's glory will cover only the land of Israel.

cards.text: Then the song turns a corner, from God's glory to David's own people.

cards.question: David turns to his own people now. What does he ask God to do for them?

answers.text: Save them with His right hand
Give them rain for their fields
Lead them back to their land

cards.text: David asks this so that God's beloved may be delivered. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this song's about to get a whole new voice.
Now the psalm says God has spoken from His sanctuary. Listen close, friend.

cards.question: True or false: God's first words from His sanctuary are a warning to David.

cards.text: God says, "I will triumph!" Then He says He will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth, places in Israel's own land.

cards.question: True or false: God says Gilead, a region of Israel, and Manasseh, one of Israel's tribes, are His.

cards.text: Then He names two more of Israel's tribes: "Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter."
Then God turns to Israel's neighbors, Moab and Edom: "Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal…"

cards.question: God names one more neighbor, Philistia. Over Philistia, God says He will shout in ___.

cards.text: Then David's voice comes back in with questions, like when your phone dies halfway to somewhere new. You know where you're headed, but you need somebody to GET you there.

cards.question: David asks who will lead him to Edom. He also asks who will bring him to what?

cards.text: Then David asks God, "Have You not rejected us, O God?" After God said He will triumph, that question lands HEAVY.

cards.question: True or false: David also asks God whether He will no longer march out with their armies.

cards.text: But David doesn't stop at the question. He keeps right on praying.

cards.question: David asks God for aid against the enemy. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The help of man is worthless

cards.question: David's last line says that with God they will perform with valor. What does he say God will do to their enemies?
